dispositions.statement: The 47 flagged rows in these 11 quarters are loans printed 'S + m % PIK <coupon> %' (Applitools, Sweep Purchaser, BP Purchaser, KWOR, Continental Battery / Acquisition, FPG Intermediate Holdco, Vardiman Black, BPG Holdings IV, Diligent): the whole floating coupon is paid in kind. On accruing loans the printed par grows each quarter by the coupon, not the margin (39 quarter steps on these loans: 28 nearer the coupon; 2 nearer the margin, both Vardiman 2026-03-31 at +0.96 and +0.34 pct, below even the margin, the quarter it went on non-accrual; 4 flat on non-accrual loans; 5 delayed-draw draws or repayments; pik_growth_sum.sql). Under the convention used for Kent (D-218) and Wine.com (Silver Capital), the build publishes pik_rate = the printed coupon, basis_spread = the margin and interest_rate_cash 0. The rule reads the margin printed before 'PIK' as the PIK rate and flags the difference: a rule problem, not a data error. Evidence strength: the filer's XBRL tags the margin as the PIK rate on these rows (Applitools 0.0625, Diligent 0.0842, BP Purchaser 0.055), so the corrections override the tag by inference from the printed form and par growth; 14 of these rows have no par-growth evidence of their own and rest on the printed format alone (BP Purchaser 2025-03-31, Diligent x2 and BPG 2026-06-30, Continental x4, Vardiman x6; 9 on non-accrual). Every row here prints the benchmark on its own line. 2025-09-30 is proposed separately (PD-pik_printed-1885968-5): its Continental Battery line prints no benchmark.
